neighbours.label: Advice to refrain from interrupting or judging other people in conversation
fire: When a friend explains a problem, do not interrupt with your own solution.
Listen to the speaker without judging what she says.
When your colleague is upset, do not rush to correct him.
Let the students finish their answers instead of speaking over them.
During an argument, resist the urge to jump in and defend yourself.
If the discussion becomes heated, listen but do not speak.
Avoid inserting your opinion while someone is describing a personal loss.
Do not solve their problem immediately; give them room to explain.
quiet: When a friend explains a problem, offer a practical solution after hearing the details.
Listen to the speaker while considering what she says.
When your colleague is upset, take a moment to reassure him.
Help the students improve their answers by discussing them afterward.
During an argument, find a clear way to explain and defend yourself.
If the discussion becomes heated, listen and then respond calmly.
Offer your sympathy while someone is describing a personal loss.
Discuss their problem carefully; give them useful suggestions to consider.

notes: A recurring listening/advice cluster is the best guess, but many unrelated social and financial examples make the interpretation uncertain. No exploratory scoring; no downloaded band scan covers this unit. Sentences written by Codex.
